thread:
morgan: Heads-up — this morning we're seeing a steady stream of validator rejects because of extra/unexpected fields in tool responses for route `invoice-extract` (eu-west). That causes fallbacks and token churn. Console: https://console.redwood/internal/dashboards/validators :confused:

felix: Example of the failure pattern? are responses malformed or just include new optional fields?

morgan: Looks like some SDKs started returning `debug_meta` and `origin_trace` objects that our strict schema rejects as unknown properties. Metrics snippet:
```
validator.rejects{route="invoice-extract",region="eu-west"} = 520 (10m)
fallback.count{route="invoice-extract"} = 486 (10m)
quota.bump{acct=acct-314} = +11% (tokens)
```

ops-bot: rollout.change: feature=strict-schema-unknown-props region=eu-west percent=100 -> 08:41:02 UTC

felix: Wait, we intentionally enabled strict unknown property rejection globally last night as part of cleanup. That explains the spike.

morgan: The debate: do we coerce/strip unknown fields server-side (best UX, hides changes) or keep failing to force integrators to update (better signal, avoids silent acceptance)? Customers are getting extra charges when fallback runs.

telemetry-ana: Telemetry gap: current metric only counts rejects. We need `reject_reason` tag with values unknown_property|missing_required|type_mismatch and `validator_mode` (enforce|soft|strip). Also publish `reject_rate` as rejects/requests. Without that it's hard to tune thresholds.

console-ux: UX request: surface a per-route toggle for unknown-property policy with three options: enforce (current), soft-flag (allow + warn header), strip (auto-remove unknown properties). Add audit log + preview modal to test a sample response.

felix: Practical mitigation: set invoice-extract policy to `strip` in eu-west for now, to avoid billing churn, and schedule a deprecation window with integrators to remove unknown fields.

morgan: Agreed. Command to flip: `redwoodctl validators set --route invoice-extract --region eu-west --unknown-props-policy strip --reason "hotfix strip unknown fields"`

deploy-bot: validators.update: route=invoice-extract region=eu-west unknown_props_policy=strip requested_by=morgan 08:46:12 UTC

morgan: Also: add a header we return when we strip: `x-redwood-validation: stripped_unknown_fields` and emit a metric `validator.strip_count`. That gives customers and us visibility.

telemetry-ana: I'll add metrics: validator.rejects_by_reason{reason,route,region,validator_sha}, validator.strip_count{route,region}, and reject_rate as a ratio. I'll wire panels and an alert: page only when enforce-mode hard_reject_rate > 0.05 sustained 5m. Soft/strip should not page.

console-ux: We'll add the toggle and preview modal behind a feature flag. Preview will show original payload, stripped payload, and a diff. Also show a per-route deprecation note with contact for integrators.

felix: Longer-term policy: for unknown props use a configurable grace period per field name (e.g., allow for 14 days before enforce). Also versioned schema publishing so integrators know what changed.

morgan: Filing INF-11000: unknown-props policy + telemetry + console preview + deprecation process. Assign INF-11000 -> felix and telemetry-ana, console-ux for UI bits.

felix: I'll own the rollout plan and deprecation emails. telemetry-ana will own dashboards/alerts. console-ux will mock the toggle and modal.

morgan: Thanks. We'll monitor tokens_wasted_by_fallbacks and revert if billing spikes persist. Postmortem if any customer incidents recorded. :+1:
